case_studies.title: COHORT: Collaborative Orchestration for Hardening via Offensive Replay on Emulated Topologies
case_studies.abstract: Mitigating an observed adversary in an enterprise network typically takes weeks of expert work: an analyst derives a mitigation tailored to that adversary, validates it without breaking production, and verifies it disrupts the specific attack. The procedure relies on expert judgment and cannot safely be exercised against the production network. COHORT is the first end-to-end framework to automate this procedure for deployable mitigations. It uses a multi-agent workflow to propose, implement, and refine mitigation strategies. The result is a faster and more efficient way to protect against specific attacks.

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding how large language models interact with each other in open-ended conversations, finding that they exhibit attractor-like behavior, where conversations settle into stable sets of behaviors. The researchers built a framework to study these interactions across 7 language models and 20 topics. The result shows that self-play trajectories are model-specific attractors that influence conversation partners.

case_studies.title: Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning
case_studies.abstract: World models offer a principled way to equip long-horizon LLM agents with foresight: predictions of action consequences before execution. However, unreliable foresight can be ignored, misused, or even degrade downstream decision-making. In this paper, we introduce WorldEvolver, a self-evolving world model framework that revises its deployment-time context while keeping the downstream agent and all model parameters frozen. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of unreliable foresight in long-horizon LLM agents by introducing WorldEvolver, a self-evolving world model framework that revises its context without changing the agent or model parameters. The researchers built WorldEvolver, which integrates three modules to improve foresight. The result is a more reliable world model that can improve downstream decision-making.

case_studies.title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving
case_studies.abstract: Coding agents are rapidly becoming a major application of agentic LLMs, but serving them efficiently remains challenging. Progress on this challenge requires understanding real workload patterns, yet the data needed for such analysis is largely absent. Existing public traces and benchmarks do not capture real, day-to-day coding-agent usage across multiple agents and model families for serving-system analysis. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding coding agent workloads for large language models, by building a dataset of 4,300 coding-agent sessions, resulting in a better understanding of real workload patterns. The dataset contains information on LLM steps and tool calls, which can help improve the efficiency of serving coding agents. This dataset can aid in optimizing cloud infrastructure for coding agent workloads.

case_studies.title: One-Step Gradient Delay is Not a Barrier for Large-Scale Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel LLM Pretraining
case_studies.abstract: Modern large-scale LLM pretraining benefits from utilizing Pipeline Parallelism; however, synchronous implementations leave GPUs idle during pipeline bubbles, wasting computational resources. Asynchronous Pipeline Parallelism eliminates these bubbles, maximizing throughput at the cost of gradient staleness. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient use of computational resources in large-scale language model pretraining by utilizing Asynchronous Pipeline Parallelism, building on the PipeDream-2BW schedule, and achieving maximized throughput. The result is a more efficient use of GPUs, reducing idle time. This is particularly relevant to optimizing large-scale AI model training.
